# Leadership Principles Standard Set

[← Amazon](../README.md) · [Every Amazon question](../../amazon.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/bq-leadership-principles-standard-set)

`deep-dive`

---

## Requirements

- Prepare at least one STAR story for each of the 16 LPs, with additional stories ready for the LPs that appear most often.
- Expect probing follow-ups such as "what would you change," "go into more detail," "what trade-off did you make," and "who disagreed with you."
- Connect every story to a business result supported by numbers.

## Examples

Question stems reported from 2026 Q2 loops:

- "Tell me about a situation where several workstreams competed against a short deadline."
- "Describe a disagreement with a colleague and how you worked through it."
- "What work did you take on even though it was outside your responsibilities?"
- "What difficult feedback did you receive or deliver?"
- "Tell me about a time the requirement was unclear and you had to respond."
- "When did you challenge a decision, then commit and execute anyway?"
- "Describe a high-risk choice you made without complete information."
- "Tell me about a fast choice you made in an ambiguous situation."
- "Go deep on one project and support the discussion with figures."

## Notes

- HM and Bar Raiser interviews may examine one story through five or more layers. Choose examples where you truly owned the result and can recall the precise figures.
- Some interviewers value proactive clarification ("I appreciate you asking that"); handle vague behavioral questions the same way you would handle underspecified coding prompts.
- FAR and Premium-tier teams press especially hard on "what would you change," so every story should include a believable improvement or iteration.
- Interviewers receive one to three LPs beforehand and assess whether you meet, exceed, or miss the bar for those principles. You can reuse the same story in different rounds because each interviewer applies a different lens.
- Customer Obsession functions as the practical north-star LP; include a customer result in every story, even when another LP is the stated focus.
- Keep about 80% of the story centered on first-person "I" actions. Moving too much into "we" or "the team" weakens the individual-contribution signal that Bar Raisers seek.
- Only the Bar Raiser and hiring manager can veto a candidate; they own the LP and behavioral assessment more strongly than the technical assessment.
- In MLE loops, the project deep dive and LP assessment may directly examine whether previous work had sufficient impact and scale. Know the figures for scope, users, revenue, latency, or model-quality change, rather than preparing only the technical account.
- Current VO loops include LP assessment in every technical slot, including coding and system design. Be prepared for a brief LP question at the beginning or end even if the calendar labels the session as entirely technical.

## Preparation

- Create a 16-by-2 STAR grid: two stories for each of the 16 LPs, with measurable results and an answer for what you would change.
- Rehearse the "go deep" follow-up by recording a five-minute response to the same BQ, then recording a ten-minute version.
- Practice "why Amazon" and "why this team" in advance; both continue to appear more often than many candidates expect.
- Find candidate stories by naming the three to five projects with the greatest impact in recent years, then link each project to two or three LPs it can support. Most candidates prepare too many separate LP-specific stories when one strong example can adapt to several.
- Rehearse the metric layer: commit the exact starting figure, change, and business effect for every story to memory. "Data-driven" is the specific wording used in Amazon's own preparation guidance.
- Practice a "circular narrative": begin with the problem, use the middle for your personal actions and their metrics, and finish by returning to the resolution. This withstands 10 to 15 minutes of deep probing better than a straightforward STAR recitation.
